question.text: Accounting basis for PMS performance calculation (per SEBI) is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Portfolio Manager performance is computed on an accrual / fair-value basis: income (interest, dividends) is recognised as it accrues, securities are marked to fair value, and both realised and unrealised gains/losses flow into the periodic return. This is the basis on which Time-Weighted Rate of Return (TWRR) — the SEBI-prescribed performance measure for PMS — is calculated and disclosed. The Trap: A pure cash basis would defer recognition until cash actually moves, distorting periodic returns. "Hybrid" is not the prescribed performance basis, and "mark-to-model only" understates the requirement that observable fair values be used wherever available. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook discusses TWRR/MWRR performance reporting, XIRR disclosure and APMI valuation norms for debt and money-market securities, but does not explicitly state "accrual / fair-value basis" as the accounting basis for PMS performance calculation on the pages checked. The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory PMS performance-measurement convention.
